examples.title: Blink the built-in LED
examples.description: Turn the built-in D13 LED on and off. Learn the order of statements and milliseconds.

lesson.wiring: Only the Pro Mini and USB–Serial adapter; use the built-in L / D13 LED.
lesson.observe: Turn the built-in D13 LED on and off. Learn the order of statements and milliseconds.
lesson.change: Change both wait values from 1000 to 200 ms and compare the blink rate.

examples.title: Potentiometer dims a PWM LED
examples.description: Map an A0 potentiometer reading to PWM brightness for an LED. A PWM output is required for analogWrite.

lesson.wiring: analog write: PIN D9; analog read: PIN A0; Potentiometer outer legs VCC/GND; wiper on the listed analog input. Common GND; use each module’s required supply.
lesson.observe: Map an A0 potentiometer reading to PWM brightness for an LED. A PWM output is required for analogWrite.
lesson.change: Change the map output maximum from 255 to 80 to limit LED brightness.

examples.title: Button controls an LED
examples.description: Read a button and change an LED. The input needs the pull-up or wiring described in the blocks.

lesson.wiring: Button between D2 and GND; internal pull-up is enabled. The output is the built-in D13 LED.
lesson.observe: Read a button and change an LED. The input needs the pull-up or wiring described in the blocks.
lesson.change: Swap the HIGH/LOW actions to make the LED light when the button is released.

examples.title: Traffic lights
examples.description: Run a simple red/amber/green traffic-light sequence. Each wait makes the next visible phase last longer.

lesson.wiring: Red LED D2, amber D3, green D4; each LED needs its own series resistor to GND.
lesson.observe: Run a simple red/amber/green traffic-light sequence. Each wait makes the next visible phase last longer.
lesson.change: Change the red, amber and green wait times separately.

examples.title: DS18B20 thermometer + Plotter
examples.description: Request a DS18B20 conversion without waiting, read it after 800 ms, and show a thermometer dashboard after Plotter Start.

lesson.wiring: DS18B20: PIN D2; Powered DS18B20: data needs a 4.7 kΩ pull-up to VCC. Common GND; use each module’s required supply.
lesson.observe: Request a DS18B20 conversion without waiting, read it after 800 ms, and show a thermometer dashboard after Plotter Start.
lesson.change: Warm the sensor with your fingers. Change the graph gauge bounds, keeping the 800 ms sensor interval.

examples.title: 16×2 I2C LCD hello
examples.description: Show a greeting on a 16×2 HD44780 LCD with PCF8574 I2C backpack. Check address and contrast first.

lesson.wiring: HD44780 I2C LCD: address 0x27; I2C SDA A4, SCL A5. Common GND; use each module’s required supply.
lesson.observe: Show a greeting on a 16×2 HD44780 LCD with PCF8574 I2C backpack. Check address and contrast first.
lesson.change: Edit the two text values. Row 0 is the first line; row 1 is the second.

examples.title: 16×2 LCD potentiometer
examples.description: Read a potentiometer and print the value on a 16×2 I2C LCD. Learn how repeated prints update a text display.

lesson.wiring: HD44780 I2C LCD: address 0x27; analog read: PIN A0; I2C SDA A4, SCL A5; Potentiometer outer legs VCC/GND; wiper on the listed analog input. Common GND; use each module’s required supply.
lesson.observe: Read a potentiometer and print the value on a 16×2 I2C LCD. Learn how repeated prints update a text display.
lesson.change: Turn the potentiometer. Edit the label and move its output column.

examples.title: SPI OLED uptime counter
examples.description: Count seconds on an SSD1306 SPI OLED using a named device and no framebuffer. Update with millis timing.

lesson.observe: Count seconds on an SSD1306 SPI OLED using a named device and no framebuffer. Update with millis timing.
lesson.change: Edit the heading or move the counter to another text row.

examples.title: ST7735 colour TFT text
examples.description: Print text and an analog reading on an ST7735 colour TFT over hardware SPI. Match the panel type and wiring.

lesson.wiring: ST7735 TFT: MOSI D11, SCK D13, CS D10, DC D9, RESET D8; MISO is unused. Potentiometer wiper A0, outer legs VCC/GND. Match the display’s supply and logic levels.
lesson.observe: Print text and an analog reading on an ST7735 colour TFT over hardware SPI. Match the panel type and wiring.
lesson.change: Change the foreground colour, text row or the potentiometer label.

examples.title: Find I2C device addresses
examples.description: Scan the I2C bus and print responding addresses in Monitor. Use it to discover the address of an attached module.

lesson.wiring: I2C module SDA→A4 and SCL→A5, with matching supply and common GND. Several modules can share the bus.
lesson.observe: Scan the I2C bus and print responding addresses in Monitor. Use it to discover the address of an attached module.
lesson.change: Disconnect one I2C module and scan again; its address disappears.

examples.title: 0.91-inch I2C OLED text
examples.description: Print text on a 128×32 SSD1306 I2C OLED. U8x8 sends character tiles without a full pixel framebuffer.

lesson.wiring: SSD1306 I2C OLED: address 0x3C; analog read: PIN A0; I2C SDA A4, SCL A5; Potentiometer outer legs VCC/GND; wiper on the listed analog input. Common GND; use each module’s required supply.
lesson.observe: Print text on a 128×32 SSD1306 I2C OLED. U8x8 sends character tiles without a full pixel framebuffer.
lesson.change: Edit the heading. Keep text rows within the 128×32 display height.

examples.title: Grove RGB LCD
examples.description: Use the text and RGB backlight of a Grove JHD1313 LCD. This module uses a different library from PCF8574 backpacks.

lesson.wiring: Grove JHD1313 RGB LCD: SDA→A4, SCL→A5, supply and GND.
lesson.observe: Use the text and RGB backlight of a Grove JHD1313 LCD. This module uses a different library from PCF8574 backpacks.

examples.title: Single piezo beep

examples.title: Simple piezo melody
examples.description: Play a short tune with the basic core tone blocks. Compare this blocking lesson with the nonblocking named music examples.

examples.title: DS18B20 temperature on LCD
examples.description: Read a DS18B20 temperature and show it on an I2C character LCD. Check the sensor pull-up and LCD address.

examples.title: 20×4 LCD potentiometer

lesson.wiring: lcd user init: address 0x27; analog read: PIN A0; I2C SDA A4, SCL A5; Potentiometer outer legs VCC/GND; wiper on the listed analog input. Common GND; use each module’s required supply.
lesson.observe: Show a potentiometer reading on a 20×4 LCD. Use the named LCD and buffer examples for reusable display logic.

examples.title: Servo sweep (core timer library)

examples.title: HC-SR04 distance gauge

examples.title: NeoPixel colour cycle
examples.description: Change WS2812 RGB LED colours. The strip library keeps a small colour buffer and sends it on show.

examples.title: Named 28BYJ: accelerated back and forth

examples.title: Setup, loop, function and variable

examples.title: Math operations

examples.title: Array animation with millis timing

examples.title: Local variables and 2D arrays

examples.title: Named stepper: position targets
examples.description: Declare a STEP/DIR device once, request target positions and keep servicing the loop engine until each target is reached.

examples.title: Named 20×4 I2C LCD

examples.title: Servo and distance sensor sweep

examples.title: I2C EEPROM: values and text
examples.description: Write and read typed values and text in a 24LC256 I2C EEPROM. Addresses are byte offsets, separate from its I2C bus address.

examples.title: SPI Flash: erase, write, read

examples.title: SD text file

examples.title: Radar measurements → BMP

Combined SD, sensing and motion: advanced, little stack/heap headroom on ATmega168. Compile size is not a runtime stack test.

examples.title: Continuous photocell scan: image + controls
examples.description: Choose one-way or bidirectional photocell sweeps with two hardware servos; adjust delayed sampling to align rows. The computer builds the image while the board averages scheduled ADC readings without a framebuffer.

lesson.wiring: Light-sensor/resistor divider midpoint A0; pan servo D9, tilt D10. Suitable servo supply with common GND. Both signals use Timer1 hardware PWM at 50 Hz.
lesson.observe: Choose one-way or bidirectional photocell sweeps with two hardware servos; adjust delayed sampling to align rows. The computer builds the image while the board averages scheduled ADC readings without a framebuffer.
lesson.change: Use the Parameters area or live controls: resolution, row time, averaging, gain/offset, black/white signal, brightness levels and servo pulse endpoints. Gain 100% = 1x. Accepted changes restart a clean image; Stop holds. Use Areas → Parameters to focus the editable settings.

notes: Small remaining memory margin: 30 bytes Flash and 611 bytes SRAM before stack/heap. Keep this advanced; compile success does not measure stack or dynamic allocation.

Coordinates follow commanded motion, not measured servo position. Mechanical lag and sensor response limit useful speed. The native ADC is 10-bit; 2–65536 output levels rescale its readings. Live bounds follow UART/ADC time and the PC image limit.

notes: Small remaining memory margin: 842 bytes Flash and 196 bytes SRAM before stack/heap. Keep this advanced; compile success does not measure stack or dynamic allocation.
Three-voice IRQ music shares Timer2. Each passive buzzer uses a separate output; Timer2 is unavailable for another independent engine.

examples.title: Timer1 stepper: fine speed commands
examples.description: Starts stationary. Enter a signed target pulse rate in Plotter; Timer1 ramps toward it with acceleration 5000 steps/s². The chart shows the requested rate, not measured motor speed.

lesson.wiring: TB6600 STEP signal D9, DIR D4 and common signal GND. Follow the module’s input-voltage wiring; power the motor through the driver.
lesson.observe: Starts stationary. Enter a signed target pulse rate in Plotter; Timer1 ramps toward it with acceleration 5000 steps/s². The chart shows the requested rate, not measured motor speed.
lesson.change: Enter -30000..30000 steps/s; Stop ramps to zero. Change acceleration in the device block. Adjacent high-speed requests can map to the same timer period. This sketch has almost no spare Flash.

notes: Small remaining memory margin: 24 bytes Flash and 359 bytes SRAM before stack/heap. Keep this advanced; compile success does not measure stack or dynamic allocation.
Very tight Flash budget on ATmega168. Compile after any edit; a larger header or extra library may not fit.
